title: Get workshop-ready: your AI agent on your laptop · hancrafted
description: A step-by-step guide for first-timers on Mac, Windows or Linux: open your terminal, install and sign in to your AI agent, start it in the starter folder and run your first skill, so the workshop can begin right away.

Your AI agent (1/2) Page 1 of 2 Install your AI agent Your first command: copy it, paste it into your terminal, press Enter. Help Your error Copy prompt ChatGPT Gemini Your computer Mac Windows Linux AI agent Claude Code Antigravity Codex GitHub Copilot Work laptop? Check before you install. If macOS asks for an administrator password, stop and ask IT or your workshop organizer. Use an agent and account your organization approves. Stop for company blocks or certificate errors too. Do not turn off security settings or switch networks to get around a block. Your first command Open your terminal from step 1, paste this line and press Enter. It installs your AI agent. $ curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash Copy Done looks like The installer ends with Installation complete . If a Setup notes block talks about your PATH, follow the fix it prints there. Then open a new terminal window and type claude . After the installer finishes without errors, close the terminal, open a new one and run this check: $ claude --version You see a version number, not an error. Then continue to Log in. If the command is still not recognized, open More help below. More help Official docs for Claude Code ( opens in a new tab ) Always there, even if this line ever changes. Some install pages need scrolling, so the line is here. What might happen The installer command failed? Check that your computer is selected above and that you pasted the whole line into your terminal. For a company restriction, stop and ask IT. Claude Code needs a paid Claude plan. The free plan does not include it, and the sign-in on the next Slide says so. Stuck, or red text you do not understand? Press Help at the top right and paste the error. Blocked on a company laptop? A Zscaler block page, certificate error or connection timeout may need different fixes. Ask IT to check the agent's approved sites, proxy and corporate certificate. A working browser does not prove the agent can connect. “Running scripts is disabled”, “blocked by your organization”, missing winget, or an administrator-password request: stop. Do not change execution policy, disable certificate checks or install a different tool to bypass the block. Tell IT which agent you chose, your PowerShell version, the step and the exact error. Remove tokens, personal information and confidential details before sharing an error or screenshot. Ask them to verify installation, sign-in and a harmless agent request before workshop day.

Your AI agent (2/2) Page 2 of 2 Log in Your second command starts your AI agent and signs you in. Use a new terminal window. Help Your error Copy prompt ChatGPT Gemini Your computer Mac Windows Linux AI agent Claude Code Antigravity Codex GitHub Copilot Open a new terminal window first The install may not be known to your old window. Close it, open a new one, and only then type the line below. On a Mac: press Cmd and N in Terminal, or open Terminal again. How to open a terminal, step 1 On a work laptop, use the account and sign-in route your organization approves, not a personal account to get around a denial. Otherwise use your own eligible account, never a shared one. If access is denied or a certificate error appears, stop and ask IT. Your second command Paste this line and press Enter. $ claude Copy Your browser opens on its own. If it does not, press c in the terminal to copy the link and open it yourself. The page may show a code: copy it and paste it into the terminal. Done looks like Logged in You do this once, and it stays. More help: what you will see, options, fixes 1 · In your terminal Claude Code ✻ Claude Code Opens a sign-in in your browser… 2 · In your browser Sign-in page ✻ Sign in to Claude Code Sign in Use your own account 3 · Back in your terminal Logged in You do this once, and it stays. Does it say “command not found” or “not recognized”? An old window may not know the new installation. Try a fresh window once. Still not recognized? Return to the installation step and its version check: the install may have failed or PATH may need fixing. For a company policy or certificate error, stop and ask IT. Which option do I pick? 1 . Pick this Your Claude account: Claude Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise. This is the one for people who pay for Claude. 2 . A Claude Console account, paid per use with API credits. Not for a normal subscription. 3 . A cloud platform such as Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud or Microsoft Foundry; the menu calls it “3rd-party platform”. For companies, skip it. The free Claude plan does not include Claude Code: you need a paid plan. If your browser does not open, press c to copy the link. If the page shows a code, paste it where the terminal says Paste code here if prompted . Claude Code · official login page ( opens in a new tab )

Overview Minimal still needs a way out A minimal manual, centred on real tasks, taught faster than a standard manual in a study of 64 students, but beginners still need error-recovery material, which is why every step has a Stuck? help 1 2 . Sources (2) Lazonder and van der Meij, The minimal manual: is less really more? ( opens in a new tab ) doi.org Kalyuga, Ayres, Chandler and Sweller, The Expertise Reversal Effect ( opens in a new tab ) doi.org

Open your terminal Hesitation is normal Computer anxiety is a long-studied, widespread reaction; about 80% of the 89 studies on experience found more experience went with less anxiety, and a relaxed first experience was linked to lower anxiety. No study measures fear of the terminal itself, so applying this to the terminal is an inference 1 . Sources (1) Powell, Computer anxiety: Comparison of research from the 1990s and 2000s ( opens in a new tab ) doi.org Why the command line feels scary System administrators said you cannot click your way around a command line to figure it out, and that it may be scary or overwhelming for a beginner; this is a survey quote, not a measured rate of mistakes 1 . Sources (1) Voronkov, Martucci and Lindskog, System Administrators Prefer Command Line Interfaces, Don't They? An Exploratory Study of Firewall Interfaces ( opens in a new tab ) arxiv.org Setup is the hard part Software Carpentry reports that installing software is often harder than using it, and that every new tool fails for at least one person in the room across Mac, Windows and Linux 1 . Sources (1) Wilson, Software Carpentry: lessons learned ( opens in a new tab ) doi.org Feedback builds confidence In a university Unix course with near-instant per-answer feedback, 78.2% of 2021 respondents said they had procedural Unix knowledge, against 38.8% before; the authors call this self-report possibly subjective, and the students were not solo first-timers 1 . Sources (1) Berry et al., ShellOnYou: learning by doing Unix command line ( opens in a new tab ) ctiber.github.io

What you're looking at Try it and see In a university Unix course with near-instant feedback on every attempt, 78.2% of 2021 respondents said they had procedural Unix knowledge, against 38.8% before; the authors call this self-report possibly subjective, and the students were not solo first-timers 1 . Sources (1) Berry et al., ShellOnYou: learning by doing Unix command line ( opens in a new tab ) ctiber.github.io
Your AI agent No speaker notes for this Slide.

Install your AI agent Windows prerequisites are separate checks Anthropic documents a native Windows installer without administrator rights and optional Git Bash 1 . GitHub requires PowerShell 6+, whereas Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 are separate installations 2 3 ; this guide recommends a current PowerShell 7 for Copilot. OpenAI's official Windows install command includes a process execution-policy override 4 . Google documents agy and its version check 5 . Codex's Windows sandbox source includes elevated provisioning, separate from user-scoped CLI installation 6 . These are documentation-verified instructions, not a clean-PC or managed-Windows test. Sources (6) Anthropic, Claude Code setup ( opens in a new tab ) code.claude.com GitHub, Installing Copilot CLI ( opens in a new tab ) docs.github.com Microsoft, Install PowerShell on Windows ( opens in a new tab ) learn.microsoft.com OpenAI, Codex installation ( opens in a new tab ) github.com Google, Antigravity getting started ( opens in a new tab ) antigravity.google OpenAI, Codex Windows sandbox setup ( opens in a new tab ) github.com Corporate blocks belong with IT Anthropic separates proxy, certificate and endpoint configuration 1 . GitHub discusses corporate certificate trust and Zscaler, and maintains a separate allowlist 2 3 ; this does not certify every CLI with every Zscaler deployment. Microsoft gives organizational Group Policy precedence over local execution-policy settings 4 . Stopping and asking IT is this guide's safety recommendation, not a promise that every block has one fix. Sources (4) Anthropic, Enterprise network configuration ( opens in a new tab ) code.claude.com GitHub, Copilot network settings ( opens in a new tab ) docs.github.com GitHub, Copilot allowlist reference ( opens in a new tab ) docs.github.com Microsoft, About execution policies ( opens in a new tab ) learn.microsoft.com

Log in A new terminal is one fix, not a diagnosis Anthropic documents Windows PATH troubleshooting 1 . A fresh terminal can pick up PATH changes but cannot repair a failed or blocked installation. GitHub allows organizations to disable CLI access; OpenAI and Google document organization-specific access controls 2 3 4 . A personal subscription or successful browser sign-in does not override company approval. The approved account and sign-in route take precedence over this guide's generic recommendations. Sources (4) Anthropic, Terminal configuration and PATH ( opens in a new tab ) code.claude.com GitHub, Copilot CLI prerequisites and access ( opens in a new tab ) docs.github.com OpenAI, Codex plan and enterprise access ( opens in a new tab ) help.openai.com Google, Antigravity enterprise setup ( opens in a new tab ) antigravity.google
Your folder No speaker notes for this Slide.
Download and unzip the starter folder No speaker notes for this Slide.

Start the agent inside that folder Check the folder, not the menu label Microsoft documents launching PowerShell from Explorer's address bar 1 . Terminal hosts configurable shells, so Open in Terminal does not guarantee PowerShell 7 2 . Get-Location checks the actual directory; Get-Content reads the starter file; Set-Location -LiteralPath accepts a literal path 3 4 5 . Microsoft's Windows 10 announcement documents the Shift-right-click PowerShell entry 6 ; it does not guarantee that entry on every Windows 11 or managed machine. The menu and path drawings are examples. These routes have not been tested on current managed Windows machines. Sources (6) Microsoft, Launching shells from Explorer ( opens in a new tab ) devblogs.microsoft.com Microsoft, Windows Terminal profiles ( opens in a new tab ) learn.microsoft.com Microsoft, Get-Location ( opens in a new tab ) learn.microsoft.com Microsoft, Get-Content ( opens in a new tab ) learn.microsoft.com Microsoft, Set-Location ( opens in a new tab ) learn.microsoft.com Microsoft, Windows 10 PowerShell context-menu announcement ( opens in a new tab ) blogs.windows.com A working folder is not a security boundary The vendors instruct users to start in their project directory; Google documents agy as the CLI command 1 2 . The folder helps the agent discover the workshop's files and skills, but does not mean it can access only that directory. Approve only the intended workshop folder and review commands before allowing them. Sources (2) Anthropic, Claude Code quickstart ( opens in a new tab ) code.claude.com Google, Antigravity getting started ( opens in a new tab ) antigravity.google
Your first skill No speaker notes for this Slide.

Run your first skill The prompt is a safeguard, not an error A model can be steered by text it reads, such as a web page or a project file, so OWASP recommends requiring a human to approve high-impact actions; each vendor builds that approval into its default mode 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 . Sources (7) OWASP, LLM01: Prompt Injection ( opens in a new tab ) genai.owasp.org OWASP, LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency ( opens in a new tab ) genai.owasp.org OpenAI, Codex: Agent approvals and security ( opens in a new tab ) learn.chatgpt.com Google, Gemini CLI: Policy engine ( opens in a new tab ) geminicli.com GitHub, About GitHub Copilot CLI ( opens in a new tab ) docs.github.com Google, Antigravity: Permissions ( opens in a new tab ) antigravity.google Anthropic, Claude Code: Configure permissions ( opens in a new tab ) code.claude.com Claude Code's prompt In manual mode, commands outside a built-in read-only set trigger a "Bash command" dialog asking "Do you want to proceed?" with Yes, "Yes, and don't ask again" and No. Prompt names and defaults differ by AI agent and version and change often, so recheck before showing one on screen 1 . Sources (1) Anthropic, Claude Code: Configure permissions ( opens in a new tab ) code.claude.com Why approvals are kept Anthropic says broad file access is risky especially under prompt injection; this is a vendor statement, not an independent study 1 . Sources (1) Anthropic, Making Claude Code more secure and autonomous with sandboxing ( opens in a new tab ) anthropic.com

script.text: This panel shows the speaker notes and voice script for the Slide you are reading, and follows you as you scroll. Press Alt+N to open or close it.

Your terminal 0:00 – 0:09 Hook You have never opened a terminal. By the end of this page you will have run your first skill in one. 0:09 – 0:37 Why this page I split this into one step per screen, because a long setup guide feels like a wall and a single step feels like something you can finish. Every step hands you one thing that works and the next step needs it, so when you arrive at the workshop, we can start with a grilling session right away and nobody spends the first hour on setup.

Overview 0:00 – 0:27 Four steps, one chain Here is the whole route in four steps: a terminal, an AI agent, a folder and a skill. Each step only works because the one before it works, so when the last one runs, you know the whole chain holds. It takes about twenty minutes. Tick what you already have, and the card on the right tells you which step to start at. 0:27 – 0:47 Skip what you have Tick the boxes you already have, like an installed AI agent, and the card jumps you to the first step that is still open. And if you would rather build the setup yourself than download it, the last Section is for you, so skip to the end.

Open your terminal 0:00 – 0:30 Not a personal failing If opening a terminal feels a little odd, that is a common reaction, and I would not read it as a sign that you are bad with computers. I think the fear comes from the blank window that gives you no hint what to press, and that is my hypothesis, not a proven fact. Nothing here asks you to prove anything, we only open the window and look at it. 0:30 – 0:54 One window, one cursor Pick your system in the toolbar, then open Terminal on a Mac, PowerShell on Windows, or the terminal on Linux. It takes one shortcut and a few letters. You will see a mostly empty window with a blinking cursor, and that is exactly what success looks like here. It is not frozen, it is waiting for you. 0:54 – 1:23 Stuck? Paste it If something looks different on your screen, you do not have to work it out alone. Press Help at the top right of the slide, paste what you see, and it wraps your system, your AI agent and the step into a prompt you can hand to a free ChatGPT or Gemini. Every step has that button, so asking for help is part of the route.

What you're looking at 0:00 – 0:17 Five parts This is what the window you just opened is made of, and there are only five parts: the prompt, the cursor, the command you type, the answer the computer prints, and the close button. That is the whole picture. 0:17 – 0:37 Point at anything Point at any part, or tap it, and a short explanation appears. If you prefer, use Next and Previous and walk through them one by one. The prompt says it is ready, the cursor shows where your typing lands, and the answer comes back right under your command. 0:37 – 0:54 You can't break it Here is the part I would like you to remember: you cannot break anything by looking around in here. If you ever feel lost, close the window, and everything in it ends. Open a new one whenever you like.
Your AI agent 0:00 – 0:14 Terminal done So you now have a window that waits for words. Because an empty window cannot do much on its own, the next piece is the AI agent that will live inside it.

Install your AI agent 0:00 – 0:19 Your first command This is the first command you type in your terminal. It installs your AI agent. Pick your computer and your AI agent in the toolbar, and the page shows you the exact line. Press the big Copy button, paste into your terminal and press Enter. 0:19 – 0:42 Official docs, always Next to the line is a button to the official docs of your AI agent. I give you the line so you do not have to scroll through a page that has no anchor, but the vendor is the source, so if the line ever stops working, the docs are one click away. 0:42 – 1:22 What you will see at the end At the end of the install, your terminal may ask you a question. For Codex on Mac and Linux it is Start Codex now, with y or N: type y and press Enter to go straight to the sign-in. Just pressing Enter means no, and then you open a new terminal and type codex. For GitHub Copilot, answer y if it asks to add itself to your shell file; the last line says copilot help, but you type copilot. For Claude Code you see Installation complete; open a new terminal and type claude. 1:22 – 1:49 What might happen Before installing on a work laptop, make sure your organization approves the agent and account. Administrator prompts, company blocks and certificate errors are reasons to stop and ask IT, not to change security settings. Check the Windows prerequisites shown for your agent, and use the fresh-terminal version check after installation. More help explains the common blockers. Remove confidential information from errors before sharing them.

Log in 0:00 – 0:28 Open a new terminal window Open a fresh terminal after installation so it can pick up the new command. For Copilot on Windows, use PowerShell 7. A fresh window fixes one common cause of command not found, not every cause. If the command is still missing, return to the version check in the installation step. If company policy or a certificate blocks you, ask IT rather than changing security settings. 0:28 – 0:49 Your second command Your second command starts your AI agent. Press Copy, paste it and press Enter. Your browser opens for the sign-in; if it does not, the terminal shows a link you can open yourself. Log in with your own account, not a shared one. You do this once, and it stays. 0:49 – 1:24 Which option do I pick? The sign-in asks you to choose, and the page lists the options in the order your AI agent shows them, with one marked Pick this. For Codex it is Sign in with ChatGPT, if you pay for ChatGPT. For Claude Code it is your Claude account. For GitHub Copilot you choose GitHub.com and then the device code. For Antigravity you use your personal Google Account. Afterwards you may be asked whether you trust the folder: say yes only for the starter folder.

Your folder 0:00 – 0:17 Terminal and AI agent, now the place to work You have a terminal and an AI agent, so what is missing is a place to work. An AI agent works inside one folder and reads what is there, so we give it one on purpose: the starter folder.

Download and unzip the starter folder 0:00 – 0:24 One link, one zip There is one link to one zip file. Download it, and then unzip it. On a Mac, double-click the zip. On Windows, right-click it and choose Extract All. On Linux, use Extract here in your file manager. Inside you will find the files the workshop needs, already in place, so there is nothing to assemble. 0:24 – 0:37 Where it lives Take a second to notice where the folder landed, usually in your Downloads. The next step goes into exactly this folder, so if you remember where it is, the rest is easy.

Start the agent inside that folder 0:00 – 0:32 Go in, then start Start from the extracted starter folder. On Windows, hold Shift and right-click it, then choose Open PowerShell window here. The menu drawing is an example; if yours has no such entry, open the help directly below it for another route. For Copilot, switch to the PowerShell 7 installed earlier by typing pwsh in that window first. Check that the prompt names the starter folder, then start your agent there. Trust only the intended workshop folder. 0:32 – 0:56 Same folder every time The order matters because an AI agent reads what is in the folder it starts in. That is how it will find your skill in a moment, and if you start it somewhere else, the skill is simply not there. So whenever you work with this starter folder, start the AI agent from inside it. 0:56 – 1:11 Chain so far Look at what you have. A terminal that waits, an AI agent inside it, and a folder it can read. One piece is left, and it is the one that proves all the others work.

Your first skill 0:00 – 0:17 Everything in place So everything is in place: a terminal, an AI agent and a folder. What is left is a skill, which is a small set of instructions your AI agent can follow, and running it shows that the chain is real.

Run your first skill 0:00 – 0:18 Type the skill Type the name of the skill, hancrafted-check-setup, and your AI agent reads it. Before it does anything on your computer, it stops and asks you. That pause is not an error, it is the AI agent handing the decision to you. 0:18 – 0:44 Say yes You are the one who decides here, so look at what it wants to run. For this skill, it opens one web page, and the answer is yes. If you were ever unsure what a command does, you could ask the AI agent to explain it before you approve. Would you rather have a tool that asks, or one that does not? 0:44 – 1:09 The proof Approve it, and the hancrafted homepage opens in your browser. That is the whole check, and there is nothing more to submit. You just ran a skill, so see you at the workshop, and until then, have a look around hancrafted. If the page does not open, the skill prints the link, and you can open it by hand.

The technical route 0:00 – 0:18 For people who build This last Section is for people who build, and it is optional. If you are comfortable with a terminal, you can get the same result without the starter folder by installing the pieces yourself. Everyone else can stop at the homepage.
